data.name: Irfaan
data.gender_notes: Irfaan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘arfa’ meaning 'to purify'. Irfaan is the name of an angel in Islamic tradition who is believed to be in charge of purifying the souls of martyrs. The name signifies a gentle and compassionate soul who is free from worldly desires and is devoted to spiritual growth. The name Irfaan carries the meaning “Gentle, Compassionate, Free” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Irfaan usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, compassionate, free and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Irfaan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, Compassionate, Free.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Irfaan total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Irfaan is popular in the Islamic community, found in various countries with large Muslim populations such as India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. Irfan is also the name of a prominent Sufi philosopher and poet, Sheikh Abu Nasr al-Farabi al-Irbili (d. 560/1166), known for his contributions to Islamic philosophy, mathematics, and music. The name Irfaan is a reflection of the deep respect and importance given to the ideas of spiritual purification and personal growth in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic belief, Irfaan is considered to be an angel of purification, and the name is often given to children who are believed to possess pure and noble souls. The name signifies a strong commitment to spiritual growth and a desire for inner peace and self-improvement. Irfaan is also a reminder of the importance of personal purification in the religious practices of Islam, and it encourages individuals to continually strive towards being closer to God.
